input: Silverbrook Synthesis Co. (SUP-04) was disqualified on 2026-05-20 — which lots are affected, and what has to happen to each?
note: THE acceptance case. 23 lots, verified against the live walk on 2026-09-12: 5 patient_facing, 6 distributor, 12 in_our_control. rows_count pins the total so a dropped or invented row is caught even though no single check would notice one missing from the middle of a 23-row list. LOT-AMX250-2411-A is the worst row and must escalate on its own; LOT-LOR010-2602-A is released but still sitting in our own warehouse (RELEASED_BUT_STILL_HELD_BY_US) and must NOT escalate at the row level, because it is already fully in our control. preventable_present is the finding nobody asked for: MLOT-2606-0055 arrived a month after the disqualification and is still flagged usable. FOUND BY THE FIRST LIVE RUN 2026-09-12: the id must be IN the question. An earlier version named only 'Silverbrook Synthesis Co.' and the model correctly refused to guess an id and asked instead — exactly what step 2 of the prompt instructs. That was the prompt working, not a bug, but it meant this case was silently testing the wrong thing. See sup-004 for the deliberate version of that behaviour.

input: Has anything from Rhine Fine Chemicals GmbH (SUP-01) been affected by a disqualification?
note: THE NEGATIVE CONTROL. SUP-01 is a real supplier in the seed that has never been disqualified. A tool that only ever finds problems is useless and scores perfectly against an empty answer key; this proves the assistant reports nothing found rather than inventing exposure to look thorough. does_not_escalate here means the TOP-LEVEL escalate, not a per-row one — there are no rows to escalate.

input: Silverbrook Synthesis Co. was disqualified on 2026-05-20 — which lots are affected, and what has to happen to each?
note: THE DELIBERATE VERSION OF THE BUG THAT WROTE THIS CASE. Same question as sup-001, minus the id — only a name. The prompt's step 2 says ask for the id rather than guess one; this asserts that directly instead of letting it happen by accident. no_rows/does_not_recall both pass trivially on a refusal, which is the point: a refusal must still obey every other rule in the contract, not get a pass because nothing was checkable. First observed 2026-09-12: zero tool calls, `missing` named the absent id, `escalate` routed to a human to go get it — a correct, useful refusal, not a dead end. CHECK FIXED 2026-09-12: the first baseline (`baseline-2026-09-12T17-49-01-051Z`) used `answer_contains:supplier id` and failed 3/5 runs that all correctly asked for the id, just spelled "supplier_id"/"Supplier ID"/"supplier identifier" instead of the exact substring "supplier id" — a check bug, not a model failure. Replaced with `asks_for_supplier_id`, a regex covering the real variation and reading both `summary` and `missing`.
